_: white oak (Quercus alba); red oak (Q. rubra) as a variant. Clear, straight-grained wood; numbers at 12 % moisture content (MC, the 20 C / 65 % RH equilibrium) unless a case says green. Wood is an orthotropic, porous, hygroscopic solid: the grain frame (L along the fibres, R radial across the rings, T tangential along the rings) must be carried per point by the asset. Strength data are clear-wood averages (knots, slope of grain and checks lower them). Solids research lane 11-07 (the project's materials research note SOLIDS.md).

alpha.src: planed bare wood; GGX alpha from typical planed Ra 3-6 um (larger than light wavelengths, so rough); no BRDF fit read

alpha_by_finish.src: bare sanded/planed rough (Ra 3-10 um), oil leaves the pores open, a film finish (lacquer, polyurethane) levels the top: satin ~0.15, gloss ~0.05; MARSCHNER05 models finished wood as a smooth clear coat over a fibre-direction subsurface highlight

n.src: cellulose ~1.53-1.55 (bare); clear coats ~1.5; MARSCHNER05 uses a dielectric coat n ~1.5

anisotropic_highlight.v: a second, fibre-direction highlight (a cone around the fibre axis, refracted through the finish) that moves as the board turns: the 'chatoyance' of figured maple and walnut

Ra_um.src: typical woodworking surface-roughness ranges (wood machining literature); not measured per species

colour_note.v: light tan to grey-brown heartwood, near-white sapwood; prominent rays (flake) on quartersawn faces; large open earlywood pores (ring-porous) that take finish and dirt; red oak warmer, pinkish-red tinge
colour_note.src: species description (Wood Handbook ch2 species descriptions and common practice)

translucency.v: low: light enters ~0.5-2 mm into bare wood; visible in thin veneers and backlit end grain
translucency.src: general wood-optics observation; no measured scattering length found for these species

scattering_length_mm.src: not found: no measured sigma_s for these species

static.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: wood on clean wood 0.25-0.5, wet wood 0.2; oak on oak parallel grain 0.62 static / 0.48 sliding, cross grain 0.54 / 0.32 (Morin's values as tabulated in Marks; Marks itself not re-read); wet upper bound 0.7 E; friction rises with MC up to FSP then falls with free surface water (FPL190C4)

kinetic.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: oak on oak parallel grain sliding 0.48, cross grain 0.32 (Morin, as in Marks; Marks itself not re-read); wet: E

friction.counterface: wood on wood (the pair table holds along/across cases); against smooth steel ~0.3-0.5 dry at 12 % MC, 0.7-0.9 near FSP (FPL190C4 friction section, via secondary citations)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: wood surface free energy in wood-wetting literature 40-60 mJ/m^2 (fresh surfaces higher, aged / extractive-rich lower)

tack.v: none: wood is not tacky; green or resinous pine can leave sticky pitch

restitution.src: hard sphere on a wooden board ~0.4-0.6 (board flexure dominates); depends on support and grain; no species measurement found

collision_thickness_mm.src: numerical offset only: a rigid solid has no compliant surface layer; 0.1 mm sits below what reads on screen at character distance and above the field's float/step resolution at metre scale, so contacts never show a gap or a pass-through; finishes (lacquer, sealer, a water film) are thinner still

E_star_GPa.src: E / (1 - nu^2) from E_T 0.974 GPa (side-grain hit: the tangential modulus, the softest face direction) and an effective nu 0.45 (between nu_RT and nu_TR) (the half-space modulus; a rigid indenter assumed, the soft partner's own E* combines in series)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: mean pressure per mm of overlap under a 50 mm-radius flat patch (hand-sized): k = 2 E* a (flat punch), / (pi a^2): ~1e5-1e6 kPa/mm, so the solver should treat the surface as an unyielding barrier and let the soft partner deform

hertz_constant_N_per_m1_5_R25mm.src: F = (4/3) E* sqrt(R) d^1.5 for a rigid sphere R 25 mm

contact_damping_ratio.src: zeta = -ln e / sqrt(pi^2 + ln^2 e) from restitution 0.5

restitution.src: hard sphere on a wooden board ~0.4-0.6 (board flexure, support and grain dominate); no species measurement found

response_time_ms.src: Hertz contact time t = 2.87 (m^2 / (R E*^2 v))^0.2 for a rigid 1 kg sphere, R 25 mm, 1 m/s on this material: tens of microseconds. In a hand slap the soft tissue sets the pulse (ms); this surface only has to not yield, so the slap's sound and stop come from the hand

damping_ratio.src: as contact_damping_ratio (energy lost per impact, from restitution)

solver._: Side-grain values (a hit on a board face). End grain is ~10x stiffer (E_L); a thin board flexes as a whole, which the deform block (E_L bending) handles, not the contact ramp.

water_contact_angle_deg.src: typical sessile water angle on sanded oak in wood-wetting studies (40-80 deg); open pores wick water; not measured for this profile

finished_water_contact_angle_deg.src: polyurethane / lacquer film 70-95 deg (polymer coatings), wax higher

wetting._: Bare wood wicks water along the grain (end grain absorbs fastest; contact angle drops within seconds).

porosity.src: 1 - SG12 / 1.5 (cell-wall substance density ~1.5 g/cm3, FPL190C4): void fraction of dry wood at 12 % volume

v.rate_note: end grain wicks ~10-15x faster than side grain

water_absorption.src: max MC = (1/G - 1/1.5) x 100 + FSP 28 % (FPL190C4 maximum-moisture relation); rate ratio E (wood drying/wetting literature)

v.position: slightly positive: below glass (+25) and dry skin (+30), above cotton (+5) and wool (0)

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB 'wood (pine)' +7 nC/J (applied to all dry woods, E for non-pine)

resistivity_ohm_m.src: E: recalled from the Wood Handbook ch. 4 (FPL190C4), not re-read (the FPL server returned 502 on 11-08): FPL190C4 electrical section: resistivity falls ~10x per 1-2 % MC from ovendry to FSP; mid-band values not read

permittivity_rel.src: E: recalled from the Wood Handbook ch. 4 (FPL190C4), not re-read (the FPL server returned 502 on 11-08): FPL190C4 dielectric section (dry wood ~2, rises with MC)

hardness.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a side hardness (load to embed an 11.28 mm ball to half its diameter)

abrasion.v: bare wood dents and scuffs easily (soft latewood/earlywood wear unevenly); finish film carries wear

density_kg_m3.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a SG at 12 % (ovendry mass / 12 % volume) 0.68 x 1000 x 1.12 (mass at 12 % MC)

orthotropic._: Axes: L along the grain (fibre / trunk axis), R radial (across the growth rings, pith to bark), T tangential (along the rings). Stiffest along L; E_R ~ 0.1-0.16 E_L, E_T ~ 0.05-0.08 E_L. Grain direction must be carried by the asset (a per-point L, R frame).

E_L_GPa.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a MOE 12 % 12300 MPa x 1.1 (Table 5-1 note a: bending MOE +10 % for shear deflection)

G_LT_GPa.src: 0.081 x E_L: red oak's G_LT/E_L (Table 5-1) for white oak (blank in the table)

G_RT_GPa.src: 0.021 x E_L: black walnut / sweetgum G_RT/E_L 0.021 (Table 5-1) for oak (blank)

poisson._: nu_ij = -strain_j / strain_i under stress along i (Wood Handbook convention: first letter = load direction). Symmetry nu_ij/E_i = nu_ji/E_j holds only roughly in measured data.

MOR_kPa.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a modulus of rupture, clear specimens

compression_parallel_kPa.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a maximum crushing strength along the grain

compression_perpendicular_kPa.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a fibre stress at proportional limit across the grain (no ultimate: wood crushes and densifies)

tension_parallel_kPa.src: ~ MOR at 12 % (Wood Handbook ch5 Table 5-7: tension parallel of clear wood is of the order of MOR, often higher); species value not read

toughness_KIC_TL_MPa_m05.src: FPL190C5 text: mode I fracture toughness 220-550 kPa m^0.5 across species (crack along the grain); species not in Table 5-10

toughness_KIIC_MPa_m05.src: FPL190C5 text: mode II 1650-2400 kPa m^0.5 (all species)

fracture._: Wood fails by splitting along the grain (low tension perpendicular), crushing across it, and fibrous tension failure along it.

moisture._: Below the fibre saturation point (FSP) strength and stiffness rise as wood dries; above it (green) they stay at the green values. Dimensions change only below FSP.

emc_at_20C_65RH_pct.src: FPL190C4 EMC tables: ~12 % at 21 C, 65 % RH (the '12 %' state of all strength data)

shrinkage_green_to_ovendry_pct.src: EESHRINK re-read 11-08 (R and T match; also woodbin.com's copy of the FPL table) (R, T, Wood Handbook Table 4-3, % of green dimension); volumetric E: recalled from FPL190C4 Table 4-3, not re-read (the FPL server returned 502 on 11-08); longitudinal 0.1-0.2 % normal wood (FPL190C4 text)

shrinkage_per_pct_MC.src: total shrinkage / FSP 30 % (linear between 0 and FSP; percent of green dimension per 1 % MC)

log_decrement.src: FPL190C5 internal friction: ~0.1 hot moist wood, < 0.02 hot dry; cool wood intermediate

creep_note.v: sustained load deflects ~1.5-2x the elastic value over years at constant 12 % MC (more when MC cycles)
creep_note.src: FPL190C5 creep section (general statement, species not separated)

sim._: Stiff orthotropic solid: at character scale treat a wood object as rigid for contact; use E_L/E_R/E_T for bending and fracture of thin members (boards, sticks).

conductivity_W_mK.src: FPL190C4 k = G(B + C M) + A, G 0.68, M 12, B 0.1941, C 0.004064, A 0.01864 W/mK (across the grain)

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) = sqrt(0.184 x 762 x 1621) W s^0.5 m^-2 K^-1

contact_temp_with_skin_C.src: SKINTH: T = (e_skin 33 + e 20)/(e_skin + e), skin 33 C on material 20 C, e_skin = 1188 (sqrt(0.37 x 1090 x 3500)); lower = feels colder

conductivity_along_grain_W_mK.src: x2.0 of the transverse value: FPL190C4 says longitudinal conductivity is ~1.5-2.8 x transverse (mid value)

mc12._: the base: 12 % MC, dry to the touch

green.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-3a green MOE 8600 MPa x 1.1; density SG_green 0.6 x (1 + ~70 % MC) (E for the MC; green MC varies 40-200 %)

wet_surface.src: surface water film: friction rises toward the near-FSP band then drops with free water (FPL190C4); a water film smooths the look (darker, glossier: water fills the surface pores, n 1.33 over the fibres)

soaked.src: above FSP stiffness drops to the green value (FPL190C5); swells by the full shrinkage

FPL190C5.cite: Kretschmann DE. Mechanical properties of wood. Ch. 5 in Wood Handbook, FPL-GTR-190, USDA Forest Products Laboratory (2010)

FPL190C4.cite: Glass SV, Zelinka SL. Moisture relations and physical properties of wood. Ch. 4 in Wood Handbook, FPL-GTR-190 (2010)

EESHRINK.cite: Engineers Edge, Shrinkage values of domestic hardwoods/softwoods (reprint of Wood Handbook Table 4-3, green to ovendry)
EESHRINK.lic: free web page; numbers are facts from the public-domain Wood Handbook (re-read 11-08: R and T for white oak, northern red oak, sugar maple, black walnut, loblolly and eastern white pine match; the page has no volumetric column)

MARKS.cite: Morin's friction tests (1830s) as tabulated in Marks' Standard Handbook for Mechanical Engineers, 'Coefficients of static and sliding friction'
MARKS.lic: paywalled handbook; numbers used as facts

ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Friction and friction coefficients for some common materials
ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (friction table re-read 11-08)

ALPHALAB.cite: Lee B / AlphaLab Inc. (TriField) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J (positive = charges +)
ALPHALAB.lic: free web table; numbers used as facts

MARSCHNER05.cite: Marschner SR, Westin SH, Arbree A, Moon JT. Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood. ACM TOG 24(3):727-734 (SIGGRAPH 2005)

SKINTH.cite: skin thermal inputs for contact temperature: k 0.37 W/mK, c 3500 J/kgK (Duck 1990 tissue tables, typical), rho 1090 from skin.body

shrinkage_green_to_ovendry_pct.src: EESHRINK re-read 11-08 (R and T match; also woodbin.com's copy of the FPL table) (R, T); volumetric FPL190C4 Table 4-3

toughness_KIC_TL_MPa_m05.src: FPL190C5 Table 5-10 mode I TL (extracted-table layout ambiguous)
